items.followUp: Write the SI unit of work and define it.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating watt or its symbol W.

rubric.why: Defines one watt as one joule of work done per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating 1 W = 1 J/s, or giving the equivalent definition in words.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second: 1 W = 1 J/s.

items.followUp: Use a speed-time graph to prove that v_f = v_i + at.

rubric.why: Shows or describes a speed-time graph with the initial and final velocities identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a speed-time graph or description identifying v_i at t = 0 and v_f at time t.

rubric.why: Uses the slope of the speed-time graph to represent acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the slope or gradient represents acceleration, or writing the acceleration relation.

rubric.why: Obtains the acceleration relation from the change in velocity over time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the relation or an equivalent rearrangement.

rubric.why: Rearranges the relation to the required result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and speed v on the vertical axis.
Mark the initial velocity v_i at t = 0 and the final velocity v_f at time t.
The slope of the speed-time graph is acceleration: a = (v_f − v_i)/t.

items.followUp: Find the centripetal force needed for a 0.4 kg body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m.

rubric.why: Identifies the given values in SI units, including converting the radius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.5 m, and v = 3 m s⁻¹.
Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values, with units, into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution with units.
Award 1 mark for obtaining 9 kg m s⁻².

rubric.why: States the force with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer 9 N.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v = 3 m/s.
The required centripetal force is 9 N.

items.followUp: A force of 40 N makes an angle of 60° with the x-axis. Find its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: Uses the correct relations for components when the angle is measured from the x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F_x = F cos 30° and F_y = F sin 30°, or equivalent component relations.

rubric.why: Substitutes the force and angle into the x-component relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 50 N and 30° for the x-component.
Award 1 mark for F_x ≈ 43.3 N or F_x = 25√3 N.

rubric.why: Substitutes the force and angle into the y-component relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 50 N and 30° for the y-component.

modelAnswer: Resolve the 50 N force into perpendicular components along the x- and y-axes.
The perpendicular components are 43.3 N along the x-axis and 25 N along the y-axis.
